title: Annotatio IV §.II cont.: Not full (no bread/wine) but semi-full (flesh eaten / blood drunk)
pass_a_gloss: For concerning the Sacred Supper and the sacramental presence and eating of the body and drinking of Christ’s blood, discourse is held somewhere either fully and as to the whole of these, or semi-fully and as to some part. In the former way it is open that at that place there is no discourse of the Supper and of sacramental presence and participation of Christ’s body and blood, because there is no discourse of Eucharistic bread and wine, nor of their presence or participation, which meanwhile constitute the integrating, even essential, parts of the Sacrament of the Sacred Supper and of sacramental presence and participation; but in the latter way it is no less clear that there is discourse of the same, because there is discourse of eating flesh and drinking Christ’s blood, and thus both of the chief and proper and nearest Object of the Sacred Supper, Christ’s flesh and blood, and of the chief and sacramental action of celebrating the Sacred Supper commanded by Christ, namely eating His body and drinking His blood.
pass_b_english: Supper-talk can be full (the whole) or semi-full (a part). John 6 is not full: no Eucharistic bread and wine, which are essential integrating parts of the sacrament.
It is semi-full: it does treat eating flesh and drinking blood — the Supper’s chief nearest object and the commanded sacramental action.
source_text: Enimverò de Cœna S. deque præsentia & manducatione corporis ac bibitione sanguinis Christi sacramentalibus, agitur alicubi, vel plenè & quà totum horum, vel semiplenè & qua partem aliquam. Priori modo de Cœna deque præsentia & participatione corporis & sanguinis Christi sacramentalibus, ditô loco non agi, in propatulo est, quia non agitur de pane & vino Eucharisticis, nec de horum vel præsentia, vel participatione, quæ interim Sacramenti S. Cœnæ nec non sacramentalis præsentiæ ac participationis partes integrantes, quin essentiales, constituunt; at posteriori modo de iisdem agi, non minus in aprico est, quia agitur de manducatione carnis & bibitione sanguinis Christi, eòque tùm de præcipuo S. Cœnæ & proprio & proximo Objecto, carne & sanguine Christi, tum de præcipua eaque sacramentali, Sacræ Cœnæ celebrationis imperata à Christo actione, scil. manducatione corporis & bibitione sanguinis ejus.
notes: Full vs semi-full; bread/wine vs flesh/blood.
